listingTitle: Audit locked Rust dependencies in CI
title: Audit locked Rust dependencies in CI
why: A committed Cargo lockfile can retain dependencies with published security advisories unless CI checks it against an advisory database.
suggestion: Run cargo audit or cargo deny check in CI, or add the RustSec audit-check or cargo-deny action.
limitations: Only checked-in GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure Pipelines, Jenkins, and SourceHut manifests are inspected; SourceHut paths are limited to root .build.yml and direct .builds/*.yml or .builds/*.yaml files.
Commands hidden behind repository scripts, reusable workflows, aliases, or nonstandard shell wrappers are not resolved.
The rule recognizes audit configuration but does not validate advisory database freshness or enforcement settings.

SourceHut evidence comes only from direct commands in tasks script scalars, not task names, packages, environment values, comments, or descriptions; YAML aliases and shell expansion or multiline command reconstruction are not resolved.
